roles.title: Machine Learning Researcher
roles.eligibility: PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning or a related quantitative field, OR 2-3 years of AI research experience. No graduation-year gate.
roles.requirements: Python + deep learning frameworks, PyTorch preferred | End-to-end model development: dataset construction, training, evaluation, profiling, monitoring | Modern architectures: MoEs, long-context transformers, VLMs, efficient attention | Distributed training (PyTorch Distributed, DeepSpeed, FSDP, Megatron-LM) | Performant, maintainable engineering code | Plus: LLM inference optimisation, CUDA/GPU optimisation, Ray or Kubernetes, RLHF/RLAIF/DPO
roles.notes: Strongest fit on the board for this candidate: newly established quant research team building AI-based alpha models; explicitly lists CUDA/GPU optimisation and LLM inference optimisation as preferred, which maps directly onto the llama.cpp kernel work. The 'PhD OR 2-3 years AI research experience' alternative means the MSc + papers + ~18 months industry route is viable, though 2-3 years is close to the line for a mid-2027 start. EU citizen, no sponsorship needed in Paris. No French-language requirement stated on this posting (unlike several other Paris reqs).

roles.title: ML platform Engineer
roles.eligibility: No years-of-experience or graduation-year gate stated; posting explicitly encourages candidates who do not meet every listed requirement to apply. Mentoring of junior team members is a listed responsibility, implying a mid/senior expectation.
roles.requirements: Strong Python engineering and software development best practices | Production experience with CI/CD and monitoring | Containers and Linux/UNIX | AWS deployment | Working knowledge of C++ for debugging components | Large-scale time series | Plus: Triton inference server, ML systems operation, platform architecture
roles.notes: ML infrastructure rather than modelling: build the tooling that the 100+ researcher org uses across the ML lifecycle. Python-first with C++ only for debugging, so it uses less of the candidate's systems depth than the ML Researcher req. No French requirement stated.

roles.title: Quantitative Economics researcher
roles.eligibility: PhD in Economics required, plus post-PhD experience (academic or private-sector research) mandatory. Candidate does not meet this gate.
roles.requirements: PhD in Economics | Post-PhD research experience | Working understanding of ML algorithms, able to modify them | Applied ML/econometrics on large datasets | Python | Strong interest in finance; no prior finance experience required
roles.notes: Hard PhD-in-Economics gate — listed for completeness, not a fit. Part of the 100+ researcher team working with data engineers and software engineers.

roles.title: Expert Data Scientist Macroeconomics - 8 years minimum
roles.eligibility: Minimum 8 years of experience in data manipulation and model building in a production environment — stated in the job title itself. Candidate does not meet this gate.
roles.requirements: 8+ years production data science | Macroeconomic data expertise | Statistics, time series, ML forecasting | Python data stack (numpy, pandas, polars, scikit-learn) | AWS | Professional English
roles.notes: Seniority-gated out. Included so the row is not mistaken for an open junior research seat.

roles.title: Product Specialist / Quant Analyst
roles.eligibility: Master's in a quantitative discipline; 'a first experience in quantitative analytics, engineering, data science or a related technical role would be beneficial'. Genuinely open to a junior profile.
roles.requirements: MSc in Statistics, Financial Engineering, ML or similar | Python with data analysis/visualisation libraries | SQL/Oracle preferred | AI/ML frameworks and generative AI | Portfolio analytics, simulations, financial modelling | Strong communication under deadlines
roles.notes: Client-facing: works with Research and Sales, delivers technical analysis to prospective clients. Quantitative in content but it is an investor-relations-adjacent seat, not an alpha research seat — the lowest-gate CFM role but likely the wrong career track for this candidate.

roles.title: Senior Quantitative Developer
roles.eligibility: 'Minimum 5 years of proven expertise in the development of trading automatons'. Candidate will have ~18 months at a mid-2027 start — does not meet the stated gate.
roles.requirements: 5+ years building trading automatons | Real-time, low-latency C++ | Market data systems (preferred) | Fluency in both French and English | Collaboration with researchers on systematic execution strategies
roles.notes: Team: Trading Core & Model Technology. The most C++-native role at CFM and the closest match to the candidate's production C++ background, but double-gated: 5 years of trading-systems experience AND French fluency required.

roles.title: Senior Quantitative Developer - Volatility
roles.eligibility: 'At least 8+ years of experience in quantitative finance, with a strong focus on options and volatility'. Candidate does not meet this gate.
roles.requirements: 8+ years quant finance, options/volatility focus | Top engineering school or BSc/MSc in Maths, CS, Physics | Python required; C++ or Rust a plus | Linux development | Pandas, Spark or Polars | AWS a plus | Professional English (no French requirement stated)
roles.notes: Despite the 'Quantitative Developer' title this is Python-first data infrastructure in the Data and Technology department; C++/Rust is only 'a plus'. Seniority-gated out.

roles.title: Quantitative Developer - Equity & Options Portfolio Construction
roles.eligibility: 4 to 8 years as a quantitative developer in financial institutions; Master's in CS, Engineering or Applied Mathematics. Candidate below the 4-year floor.
roles.requirements: 4-8 years quant dev in financial institutions | MSc in CS/Engineering/Applied Maths | Strong Python and scientific stack: Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn | Systematic equity and options portfolio construction | Backtesting frameworks | French and English both required
roles.notes: Portfolio Construction team in the Equity Pole. Python-only stack despite the C++-track title; French required. Experience floor and language requirement both bind.

roles.title: Senior Software Engineer
roles.eligibility: Minimum 5 years of Python development plus AWS infrastructure experience. Candidate below the stated floor.
roles.requirements: 5+ years Python | AWS infrastructure | C++ and/or Angular/React ideally | Developer-experience tooling, cross-team integration | Interest in code quality and testing
roles.notes: Data and Technology department, developer-experience/platform work rather than trading systems. C++ is optional here.

roles.title: Market Risk Quant
roles.eligibility: 'Masters or PhD (or similar) in a quantitative subject such as Mathematics, Physics, Statistics, Economics, or Finance'. No years-of-experience floor and no graduation-year gate stated — the only CFM in-scope role with no seniority bar.
roles.requirements: MSc or PhD in a quantitative subject | Advanced Python: pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn | SQL | Understanding of financial products across asset classes | Risk monitoring, limit management, dashboards, stakeholder reporting | Preferred: equity factor models, systematic trading strategies
roles.notes: Only London opening on the board and the only in-scope role with no explicit experience floor. Posting states frequent visits to the Paris office. Risk-function seat rather than alpha research, and Python/SQL-centric — no C++ or ML content. UK: HPI visa is self-sponsored, so no cost to CFM; the posting states nothing about sponsorship.

existing_rows_audit.detail: The generic Paris 'Quantitative researcher' req (https://jobs.cfm.com/job/Paris-Quantitative-researcher-75/1332608055/) now returns 'Sorry, this position has been filled.' Paris research hiring is currently specialised: 'Quantitative Economics researcher' (PhD Economics + post-PhD experience required) and 'Machine Learning Researcher'. The row's claim that a junior QR intake accepts an MSc is not supported by any live CFM posting; the surviving research reqs are PhD-preferred or PhD-mandatory.

London office confirmed on CFM's own contact page (4th Floor, Almack House, 28 King Street, London SW1Y 6QW, https://www.cfm.com/cfm-contact-us/), but the only London req on https://jobs.cfm.com/search/ is 'Market Risk Quant' — no Quantitative Researcher posting exists in London as of 2026-08-04. The £120-180k figure in the row is not stated anywhere on CFM's site and should be treated as unsourced.

Out of scope for this pass (US). The New York office does exist (510 Madison Ave, Floor 29, per https://www.cfm.com/cfm-contact-us/) and NY reqs are live on the board, but they are equity research analyst and data scientist roles, not a generic Quantitative Researcher; the $250-350k comp figure is unsourced.

notes: Careers URL correction: https://www.cfm.com/careers/ (cited by all three existing rows) returns HTTP 404. The live board is https://jobs.cfm.com/search/ (SAP SuccessFactors), linked from https://www.cfm.com/join-us-cfm-careers/. Board had 30 total reqs on 2026-08-04; all were enumerated across two pages and every in-scope posting listed above was opened and read individually. Offices: CFM's own contact page lists only Paris, New York, London, Toronto and Shanghai — Tokyo and Sydney addresses appear only in secondary sources (LinkedIn/aggregators) and are NOT on CFM's own site, so do not assume a Tokyo seat. Shanghai office is confirmed on CFM's own page but has zero postings on the board; two China-facing roles (China Data Sourcing Specialist, China Alpha Capture Relationship Manager) are posted as Paris-based and are sales/data-sourcing, so out of track. No Singapore or Hong Kong presence. Compensation: CFM publishes no salary figures on any posting; every comp_local is deliberately empty. Track skew worth flagging: CFM's Paris engineering reqs use 'Quantitative Developer' titles but are overwhelmingly Python/AWS — only 'Senior Quantitative Developer' (Trading Core & Model Technology) is genuinely low-latency C++, and it requires 5 years of trading-automaton experience plus French fluency. Three Paris reqs (Senior Quantitative Developer, Quantitative Developer - Equity & Options) explicitly require French as well as English. Excluded as out of track after review: Senior Merger Arbitrage Analyst (Paris, discretionary/fundamental M&A analysis, not quant), Research operations, Data Support & Reliability Engineer, NetOps/DevSecOps/GenAI Security/Senior Security Operations engineers, Treasury, Business Controller, Hedge Fund Operations, and four front-end/middle-office internships. Net picture for this candidate: only two of ten in-scope roles clear the eligibility gates — Machine Learning Researcher (Paris) and Market Risk Quant (London) — with the Paris ML Researcher the clear best fit on content.
